rv.q: As for me, I might warm more to “November” if it were a musical.

Nathan Lane is back on Broadway in David Mamet's 'November,' playing a corrupt president with the playwright's trademark profanity-laced dialogue, but the comedy feels more like a sketch stretched thin than a fully realized theatrical work.
Mamet’s farce does provide Nathan Lane with a dazzling showcase for the actor’s comic gifts.

tn.cat: Best Featured Actress in a Play

cn.t: Nathan Lane delivers a brilliant comic performance in Mamet's political satire, but critics are divided on whether the slight material rises above a stretched-out sketch, despite sharp direction and laughs.
